newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher on rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher on rate cut hopes.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Tuesday on investors' expectations that the Bank of Israel will reduce its key lending rate, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.49 percent, or 1.30 points, to 265.34 on all-share turnover of 135 million shekels against 126 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.70 percent higher at 273.54.
The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its interest rate to 13.9 percent at the end of February.
"The market is very positive and the success of the first part of the public offering (to institutional investors) of Bank Leumi is very encouarging," said Ron Weisberg at IBI Investment House.
IBI said on Tuesday that the Israeli government will increase the size of a Bank Leumi public offering to $150 million in shares and warrants from $125 million.

Some 20 European institutional investors have pre-commmitted to purchasing $120 million worth of shares and warrants. A further $30 million worth will be sold in the offering open to the general public, on May 27.
Bank Leumi shares lost 2.0 percent to 530 agorot. Traders said that the shares declined because they were offered to institutional investors at a minimum price of five shekels.

"Investors are optimistic and the positive trend is expected to continue. Stocks are expected to offer nice yields considering the fact the interest rate will further decline in the next few months as the economy slows down," said Doron Tsur head of research at Sahar Securities.
Tsur said that bonds and other fixed-income investments will become less attractive in the long term.

Weisberg added that the Bank of Israel might decide next Monday on a moderate rate cut only. "I believe that the market will not rise much further before Tuesday as investors wait for the rate decision and offering of Bank Leumi," he said.

Clal Electronics Industries gained 2.5 percent to 40,873 agorot. The company said on Tuesday that earnings per share in the first quarter of 1997 fell to 3.22 shekels from 25.49 shekels a year earlier.

The First International Bank rose 1.5 percent to 254,800 agorot. The bank said on Tuesday that earnings per share in the first quarter rose to 9.17 shekels from 7.57 shekels in the same period last year.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which fell 0.75 percent to 359 agorot on volume of 12.3 million shekels; Delek, which lost 1.0 percent to 10,429 agorot on turnover of 5.7 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which lost 0.25 percent to 29,840 agorot on turnover of 5.6 million shekels.
